findings.detail: In a default stdout Scrut block, `\exec 1>/dev/null; some-command 2>&1` bypasses the guard. Bash resolves `\exec` to the exec builtin, but `plain` returns null for literal words containing backslashes. Consequently, changes_shell_stdout misses the persistent redirect, and the later stderr merge is exempted as live forwarding although it writes to /dev/null. This is additional to the accepted saved-alias and composed-prefix cases.
findings.fix: Decode statically escaped command names before recognizing exec, or conservatively withhold live-forwarding exemptions when a command name is unresolved and redirects stdout. Add a static regression case for escaped exec.
findings.title: write-bash-scripts: Checked commands: Escaped exec names bypass stdout-change detection.

strengths: AST parsing distinguishes actual redirects and comments from quoted text.
Static regression samples exercise rejection without executing sample programs.
summary: Reviewed the committed scope and found one additional Important guard bypass. The two explicitly accepted limits remain separate and are not re-reported. No files were changed, and no repository code or mechanical checks were run.
